description: Hello fellow citizens of earth, we are MunanKi and we represent the love of expression in all forms. From the littlest flower to the biggest constellation, art can be found in every corner of the galaxy. And here we are, sharing a part of our innovation and artistic talents with the you. We are looking forward to this great event. Thank you for reading
summary: Decades of pioneering space exploration have left inactive spacecraft scattered across the Moon, Mars, and deep space, often misunderstood as mere space debris while remaining inaccessible to non-English-speaking and other communities due to language barriers. To preserve humanity's off-world technological heritage for the "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" challenge, our goal is to transform historical NASA hardware into an engaging, multicultural educational journey.   We developed an interactive, multilingual web storytelling experience following Rawa, a curious 15-year-old girl from the Andean mountains of Cajamarca, Peru. Using her portable telescope, hand-painted visuals, synchronized voice narration, and optical focusing mini-games, users explore inactive missions—from Apollo Lunar Modules, ALSEP stations, and Laser Retroreflectors to Mars rovers (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity), Viking orbiters, and interstellar probes—available in English, Spanish, and Quechua on both desktop and mobile devices. We want children to see themselves in Rawa and feel inspired to explore beyond this world.
details:
1. How It Works & What It Does Our project is an interactive digital storybook featuring synchronized voice narration, multilingual support (English, Spanish, and Quechua), and hands-on mini-games. Designed for both desktop and mobile devices, the experience guides users through an orbital menu where they calibrate optical lenses and capture archival snapshots to uncover the history of inactive NASA spacecraft across the Moon, Mars, and deep space—including Apollo Lunar Modules, ALSEP stations, Laser Retroreflectors, Mars rovers, and Viking orbiters.

2. IMPACT, BENEFITS & SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDGs)

  • Social, Environmental & Technological Benefits:
    • Social: Democratizes space science and preserves indigenous linguistic heritage by integrating Quechua alongside Spanish and English. We want children to see themselves in Rawa and feel inspired to explore beyond this world.
    • Environmental: Promotes zero-waste digital education and raises awareness about orbital stewardship and space heritage preservation rather than treating historic hardware as mere debris.
    • Technological: Delivers a lightweight, accessible web experience requiring no heavy downloads or high-end hardware, optimized for mobile devices in rural areas.
  • Contribution to UN SDGs & NASA Missions: Directly supports SDG 4 (Quality Education) by providing inclusive STEM learning resources, and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) by bridging the gap for underrepresented Andean and non-English-speaking youth. It aligns with NASA’s strategic goals for public engagement, Artemis lunar heritage preservation, and planetary science outreach.
  • Expected Community Impact: Empowers students and educators in Cajamarca and across Latin America with an engaging storytelling tool that connects local cultural identity with global space exploration.

3. OBJECTIVES & EXPECTED RESULTS

  • General Objective: Transform historical NASA mission data into an emotionally resonant, interactive educational journey that honors humanity’s off-world technological legacy.
  • Expected Results: A fully functional, responsive web storybook featuring 23+ narrative scenes, interactive optical calibration mechanics, multi-language voice synthesis, and an archival gallery connecting users directly to official NASA repositories.

4. METHODOLOGY, WORK PLAN & PROJECT MANAGEMENT

  • Project Phases & Deliverables:
    • Phase 1 (Ideation & Data Curation): Selection of historic NASA missions across the Moon, Mars, and deep space; verification of telemetry and historical facts. Deliverable: Technical script and mission database in Google Docs.
    • Phase 2 (Visual Art & UI/UX Design): Character design of Rawa, Andean framing, layered paper-cut backgrounds, and custom riveted metallic UI buttons. Deliverable: Hand-painted .webp and .png assets in Clip Studio Paint.
    • Phase 3 (Web Development & Localization): Coding responsive layouts, parallax animations, camera blur/focus mini-games, and Spanish/English/Quechua voice narration. Deliverable: Functional web prototype.
    • Phase 4 (Testing & Pitch Production): Cross-device mobile testing and video editing. Deliverable: Final web deployment and pitch video in After Effects.
    • Fabiana Cerquín - Main brainstorming, ideas, creatives names and interactions. Rough sketches for our character and worldbuilding.
    • Alejandra Tirado – Creative Direction, Character Design, Hand and Digital-Painted Art & UI Assets. Video Editing (After Effects)
    • Lucía Urbina– General direction, Technical Scriptwriting, NASA Data Research & Multilingual Localization (ES/EN/QU). Testing & Documentation.

5. TECHNICAL STACK & TRANSPARENCY ON AI USAGE

  • Tools & Software: Google Docs & Notes (scripting/research), Clip Studio Paint (hand-drawn digital illustration), Antigravity (assisted coding environment), Adobe After Effects (video presentation).
  • Programming Languages: HTML5, CSS3 (fluid responsive queries), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6) utilizing the native Web Speech API (speechSynthesis) and Web Audio API.
  • Hardware: Standard laptops, graphic drawing tablets for manual illustration, and smartphones for responsive touch testing.
  • Use of Artificial Intelligence: Because our story celebrates human ingenuity and craftsmanship, 100% of our visual art, character designs, paper-cut layers, UI buttons, and narrative script were created manually by humans—with zero AI-generated imagery. AI tools (Antigravity and LLM assistance) were used strictly for code structuring, CSS responsive debugging, and English/Quechua translation refinement.

6. CONCLUSIONS & FUTURE IMPROVEMENTS

  • Lessons Learned: Combining cultural storytelling with tactile mini-games significantly increases engagement compared to static text archives.
  • Future Optimizations: Recording native human voice actors for the Quechua and Spanish narrations, adding an offline Progressive Web App (PWA) mode for rural schools without stable internet, and expanding the telescope menu with 3D interactive spacecraft models.

7. NASA OPEN DATA & SPACE AGENCY PARTNERS

  • NASA Data & Mission Resources Used:
    • NASA Science – Moon & Apollo Missions (ALSEP & Lunar Laser Ranging): [https://science.nasa.gov/moon/](https://science.nasa.gov/moon/)
    • NASA Mars Exploration Program (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity): [https://mars.nasa.gov/](https://mars.nasa.gov/)
    • NASA Solar System & Deep Space Missions (Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 & 11, Kepler): [https://science.nasa.gov/missions/](https://science.nasa.gov/missions/)

8. ANNEXES

  • Working, scripting
